newsitem.title: UK: T&N sees profit margins recovering.
newsitem.headline: T&N sees profit margins recovering.

text.p: Vehicle engine components manufacturer T&N Plc's chairman said he was not worried about a fall in operating margins last year since he was confident they were now recovering.
The company said that operating margins fell to 9.1 percent last year from 11 percent in 1995 due to a combination of job cuts, de-stocking of finished products to boost cashflow and price pressures.

"We do think this is the bottom and we already have in place new efficiency improvements, new (cost) reductions which ensure those margins will be coming back from now," Colin Hope told Reuters in an interview.
"We believe that at the peak of the cycle the group should be able to achieve 12 percent-plus (margins)...12 percent at the peak and certainly an average 10 percent over the cycle," he said.

Hope said price-cutting and rationalisation had hit margins in some product areas, while a move to cut stocks had hit production efficiencies. Stock levels were cut by 25 million in 1996, making a reduction of 55 million stg in the last 18 months, Hope said. "It is very difficult to maintain margins at quite the level they were because taking stocks down at that rate does have some cost effects," he said.

T&N earlier announced it made a pretax loss of 388 million stg for 1996, after setting up nearly a billion stg of provisions and insurance to protect it from the legacy of its past existence as the Turner & Newall asbestos mining and materials business.

The company said operating profits from continuing operations before exceptional charges fell to 178 million stg from 227 million in 1995 on sales from continuing businesses of 1.89 billion stg, compared with 1.85 billion stg in 1995.

Redundancies cost 15 million against 11 million stg in 1995 and T&N said more cuts were expected this year as it expected to see a five percent fall in the workforce in 1997. --Greg Mahlich, London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717
